_comment: Flow TCK scenario manifest (SCHEMA.md v1). planes lists which emitters run; a single-plane row is a plane-qualified family per SCHEMA.md and the RFC carries the same qualification. runs (optional) = multiple invocations of the SAME plane that must all match the expectation (env variants).

scenarios.note: Deterministic HALF of the family: sequential close-then-spawn pins the refusal semantics (reason byte). The concurrent interleaving is close_spawn_race.

The RACING half: N iterations of scope.close() racing a concurrent spawn attempt from another execution context; invariants aggregated over all iterations (admitted children never lost, refused handles always resolve, close always completes). The timing-dependent admitted/refused split is emitted as debug.* records only (driver-dropped).

scenarios.qualification: Restart supervision is a Rust-plane capability (D2); C++ Supervision has no kRestart.
Restart supervision is a Rust-plane capability (D2); C++ Supervision has no kRestart.
Rust prevents stale handle reuse structurally (join/await consume by move); the runtime-observable second-consume refusal exists only on the C++ plane.
Lane pool + rollback executor are C++-plane surfaces (Rust runs on tokio; no lanes).

Counter TIER is plane-native (Rust event-queue AdmissionStats vs C++ lane-pool LaneStats — a differentiated-scheduler consequence); the emitted records use unified logical names (admission_refused, deadline_dropped) derived from each plane's observed native counters, so the expectation stays single-file.
